subtle.$description: subtle interactive fill — one step darker than surface (hover rows, selection, hover chips); mirrors --color-text-subtle (#174)

elevated.$description: white — floats above surface (gray-100) via shadow

code.$description: In light mode: dark navy block (inverted) — no border needed, bg does the work. In dark mode: deep navy tint + explicit border — bg alone can't delineate at low L. — navy-800 on white page

subtle.$description: OKCA 5.0 on page ✅ — gray-500 (L=0.56) was OKCA 3.8; stepped to L=0.50 for OKCA compliance (#14)

subtle-on-surface.$description: OKCA 5.0 on bg-surface ✅ — gray-600 (L=0.46) was OKCA 4.5 on gray-100; stepped to L=0.44 (#14)

subtle-on-inverse.$description: OKCA 6.0 on bg-inverse ✅ — muted links on dark nav/tabs

message.$description: Component-scoped: toast message text validated against status backgrounds — dark on light status-bgs ✅

on-inverse.$description: subtle divider on navy-800 inverse surface

control.$description: Form control boundaries must meet WCAG 1.4.11 non-text contrast (3:1 OKCA). gray-500: OKCA 3.8 on page ✅, OKCA 2.8 on bg-surface ❌ — use --color-border-control-on-surface on any container that hosts form controls on a surface bg. Declared light-only and aliasing the primitive, so dark inherits the same L=0.56 grey: OKCA 3.5 on dark page ✅, OKCA 2.9 on dark bg-surface ❌ — the same split as light, which is why only the -on-surface sibling needs a dark value (#217).

control-on-surface.$description: OKCA 3.8 on bg-surface ✅, OKCA 5.0 on page ✅

thumb.$description: Form-control knob fill (slider/switch thumb) — a light puck; pairs with --color-border-control (darker) for the edge. icon/border use (non-text UI). — white knob in light — icon/border use

destructive.$description: Boosted chroma from the existing burgundy hue — signals irreversibility. Distinct from error (H=25 orange-red): destructive = a chosen action, not a failure state. Both modes: outlined — transparent bg, crimson border+text. Hierarchy mirrors dark mode.

destructive-text.$description: OKCA 9.3 on page ✅, OKCA 6.9 on bg-surface ✅ — outlined, so both backgrounds are real placements (#224)

destructive-border.$description: matches text — no separate pairing: identical value, and a border's 3.0 non-text floor is strictly below the text floor already measured

tertiary.$description: No border — structural identity is the fill (distinct from secondary's outline). — was gray-100; bumped for visibility without border

link.$description: azure-400 is the brand original (#1493FB) — use on dark backgrounds only. azure-500/600 are the accessible steps for use on white backgrounds. — OKCA 5.3 on white ✅ — azure-500 (L=0.53) was OKCA 4.4; stepped to L=0.49 for OKCA compliance (#14)

link-visited.$description: OKCA 5.8 on white ✅ — honors universal :visited convention

highlight.$description: Inline code — burgundy-700, clearly distinct from indigo visited links (ΔE 0 collision fixed). — OKCA 6.9 on bg-surface ✅, OKCA 9.3 on page ✅

error.$description: Base colors: non-text use only (icons, borders, indicators). For text on light status-bg, use --color-status-*-text (contrast-validated below). — icon/border use — OKCA 3.6 on error-bg ✅ (WCAG 1.4.11)

error-text.$description: OKCA 5.4 on error-bg ✅ — C=0.22 exceeded what sRGB holds at this L and H, so the token specified no single colour and its recorded 4.6 was undefined; re-authored to the boundary, same L and H (#225)

success-text.$description: OKCA 5.1 on success-bg ✅ — L=0.50 was OKCA 4.2; stepped to L=0.46 (#14)

warning-text.$description: OKCA 6.9 on warning-bg ✅ — C=0.16 was the furthest outside sRGB of any Candor colour (deltaE 11 from the nearest in-gamut form, and off-hue with it — amber becoming dark red); re-authored to the boundary, same L and H (#225)

text.$description: inherits OKCA 5.0 on bg-surface ✅ (dark resolves to 5.6)

bg.$description: Indigo wash + decorative indigo left border, tying back to the #6969F7 anchor. — light indigo wash — text-default OKCA 10.4 on this bg ✅

highlight-decorative.$description: icon/border use — decorative accent below every text threshold; never a color: value (#132)

subtle.$description: subtle interactive fill — a hair lighter than surface in dark (direction flips vs light) (#174). Cooled counterpart of gray-700 so it recedes on the cool-navy surfaces instead of advancing (warm advances / cool recedes); L preserved.

elevated.$description: one step above surface — matches cool undertone

code.$description: Deep navy tint — hue-distinct from gray-900 page but not light-inverted. Border required: bg-to-page contrast is ~1:1 at these low L values. — text-default OKCA 11.9 on this bg ✅ — code text inherits it

default.$description: OKCA 12.9 on bg-page ✅ — off-white with cool undertone; white OKCA 19.2 on bg-page is harsh

disabled.$description: OKCA 2.2 on bg-page — intentionally below AA (1.4.3-exempt; see #134)

subtle-on-inverse.$description: muted text on white inverse surface

on-action.$description: OKCA 7.0 on action-primary ✅ — same as bg-page; gray-800 (L=0.24) was OKCA 5.6, fails 14px bold threshold of 6.5

message.$description: Component-scoped: toast message text on the three dark status backgrounds. Written out per background rather than as a range — it was OKCA 5.5–5.8 across all three, and the audit's grammar has no range form, so that phrasing was unverifiable and had never once been measured (#224). — OKCA 5.8 on error-bg ✅, OKCA 5.8 on success-bg ✅, OKCA 5.5 on warning-bg ✅ — intentionally subtle in dark mode; dimming is a feature, not a bug

on-inverse.$description: subtle divider on white inverse surface

control.$description: Form control boundaries must meet WCAG 1.4.11 non-text contrast (3:1 OKCA). gray-500: OKCA 3.8 on page ✅, OKCA 2.8 on bg-surface ❌ — use --color-border-control-on-surface on any container that hosts form controls on a surface bg. Declared light-only and aliasing the primitive, so dark inherits the same L=0.56 grey: OKCA 3.5 on dark page ✅, OKCA 2.9 on dark bg-surface ❌ — the same split as light, which is why only the -on-surface sibling needs a dark value (#217).

control-on-surface.$description: L=0.60: OKCA 4.2 on dark page ✅, OKCA 3.5 on dark bg-surface ✅

thumb.$description: Light puck on the dark track — fill stays light (border-control 0.56 is the darker edge). icon/border use (non-text UI). — oklch(0.91) light knob in dark — icon/border use

primary.$description: Direct OKLCH values instead of navy-* scale refs — the navy palette is intentionally low-chroma (C≤0.06) which reads as muted gray-blue at light steps. Boosted chroma (C=0.11 — the most sRGB renders at this L and hue) makes the primary button read as a confident blue without changing hue or breaking contrast targets. Deliberately no figures here. Both that this comment used to carry were duplicates recorded better elsewhere, and one had gone stale unnoticed because the export discarded this comment entirely (#224): it credited the label as gray-800, which was OKCA 5.6 here, but the label stopped being gray-800 when --color-text-on-action moved to the bg-page navy for exactly that reason — it fails the 14px bold floor of 6.5. That token's own comment records the change and is audited; this one restated it and rotted. — OKCA 7.3 on bg-page ✅

secondary.$description: Label on the secondary fill: bg-page OKCA 7.3 on this bg ✅ — OKCA 7.6 on bg-page ✅ (fill vs page)

destructive.$description: Outlined — same pattern as light mode, lighter crimson-rose for dark bg. H=347 at high lightness reads as pink filled; outlined avoids the fill entirely.

destructive-text.$description: Stepped L=0.75 → 0.78 so the label clears its floor on BOTH backgrounds, not only the page. The button is outlined (transparent fill), so its effective background is whatever sits behind it — and a destructive confirmation most often sits in a modal or card, i.e. on bg-surface. L=0.75 measured 3.9 there against a 4.5 floor while passing on page at 4.7, so the variant failed in its commonest placement and the single page-only pairing could not see it (#224). deltaE 3 from L=0.75 — at the edge of imperceptible. — OKCA 5.6 on bg-page ✅, OKCA 4.7 on bg-surface ✅ — Tier 2 floor 4.5; L=0.74 was OKCA 4.4 on bg-page (#209), L=0.75 was OKCA 3.9 on bg-surface (#224)

destructive-border.$description: matches text — no separate pairing: identical value, and a border's 3.0 non-text floor is strictly below the text floor already measured

tertiary.$description: ⚠️  fill is only OKCA 1.1 on page — intentionally subtle in dark mode. Text (gray-0) on tertiary bg remains readable. Uses the cool-gray ramp (matching bg-subtle) so tertiary recedes on the cool-navy surfaces instead of advancing and competing with the primary button (warm advances / cool recedes); L preserved, so white OKCA 12.0 on this bg ✅. Revisit if buttons need more prominence in dark. — cooled counterpart of gray-700

highlight.$description: burgundy-200 — inline code on the dark ramp. — OKCA 9.7 on bg-surface ✅, OKCA 11.6 on bg-page ✅

error.$description: Lightened foreground colors to meet contrast on dark backgrounds. Backgrounds mirror light-mode approach: near-neutral dark surface (C≈0.02), letting the border/icon carry the full color signal. High-chroma fills were competing with vivid borders and creating a "glowing" effect. — icon/border use — not required to pass text contrast

error-text.$description: OKCA 6.0 on error-bg ✅ — C=0.22 was far outside sRGB, so the token named no single colour and every figure recorded for it was undefined; its nearest in-gamut form was OKCA 3.4, which is how five failures sat inside a passing audit (#222). Re-authored to the boundary, same L and H (#225). L=0.77 was OKCA 4.2; stepped to L=0.79 (#14) — a step taken against the unrenderable value, kept because it still holds for the renderable one

success.$description: icon/border use — not required to pass text contrast

warning.$description: icon/border use — not required to pass text contrast

warning-text.$description: OKCA 6.8 on warning-bg ✅ — C=0.16 exceeded what sRGB holds at this L and H; re-authored to the boundary, same L and H (#225)

text.$description: inherits OKCA 5.0 on bg-surface ✅ (dark resolves to 5.6)

bg.$description: dark indigo wash — text-default OKCA 10.1 on this bg ✅

highlight-decorative.$description: icon/border use — decorative accent; never a color: value (#132)
